meeting_header: 2025-11-20 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendez (Acme Head of ML), Aisha Khan (Acme Platform Lead), Tom Wu (Acme CTO)
summary: AE+SE walked through final POC success criteria and acceptance tests. Agreed on a benchmark plan (10k requests, representative token length distribution), explicit go/no-go thresholds for latency, cost, throughput, and quality (hallucination/factuality). Reporting format agreed: weekly dashboard + final signed report with raw logs, token-level cost breakdown, and per-route P95/P99 latency. Next steps: Redwood to send doc and run benchmark next week; customer to supply sample prompts and traffic profile.
topics: Success criteria: latency, throughput, cost, quality
Benchmark plan: 10k request run, token distribution, hardware variants
Security/compliance questions: SOC2, KMS, data residency
questions: What hardware will Redwood use for the benchmark?
Is the hosted option acceptable or do we need Dedicated/VPC?
What are the exact go/no-go numeric thresholds?
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: All right good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. we wanted to get final signoff on the POC success criteria and acceptance tests — quick roll call?
[00:12] Carlos Mendez: Carlos here, Aisha here as well, Tom is on.
[00:16] Priya Raman: Priya from Redwood, I'll be running the benchmarks with you.
[00:20] Jordan Lee: Cool, goal for today is to lock down the go/no-go thresholds, the benchmark plan (10k requests), and reporting format so we can run a clean acceptance test next week.
[00:33] Aisha Khan: Sounds good. quick context: our production inference is currently running on a mixture of CPU and infer-optimized instances, typical request size ~350 tokens median, bursts to 1k. We care most about P95 latency under heavy load and hallucination rate on factual prompts.
[00:50] Priya Raman: ok useful. for the benchmark we'll want your traffic profile and a 500-sample eval set that highlights areas you care about e.g. financial copy, product specs. can you provide that by monday?
[01:05] Aisha Khan: yes we'll drop that in the shared drive, target by Sunday night.
[01:12] Tom Wu: a couple things from my side: we're evaluating hosted vs dedicated. security is a blocker if we can't get KMS integration or control over logs. can you confirm what you can share?
[01:25] Jordan Lee: absolutely — Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS, we can run the POC on a VPC connector if needed. we'll include the security pack (SOC2, ISO, KMS details) in the follow up.
[01:36] Carlos Mendez: great. on success criteria, we're proposing: P95 latency < 250ms for 512-token requests, throughput of at least 120 requests/min sustained, cost target <$0.10 per 1k tokens, and hallucination/factuality failure rate < 5% on the eval set. thoughts?
[01:53] Priya Raman: those are reasonable starting points. couple clarifying q's — is the 250ms target measured cold-start or steady-state?
[02:02] Carlos Mendez: steady-state under realistic batching, not cold.
[02:06] Priya Raman: ok. for the benchmark we'll run sustained traffic to warm KV caches, and then measure steady-state P50/P95/P99. we'll also run a short cold-start test.
[02:16] Jordan Lee: for quality we want measurable criteria: we'll use your 500 eval prompts and compute pass/fail based on rubric you provide. if you don't have a rubric we can propose one — e.g., factuality check (binary), hallucination tokens ratio, and semantic similarity to ground truth for classification prompts.
[02:33] Aisha Khan: we'll provide the rubric, but is there a recommended threshold for hallucination detection? 5% seems ok but we want to understand the distribution.
[02:42] Priya Raman: recommend we report both absolute failure rate and per-prompt severity buckets (high/medium/low). go/no-go is overall <5% failures and no critical prompts failing at >10%.
[02:52] Tom Wu: ok that sounds measurable. what about model variants — are you planning to run quantized models or FP16? We need to compare accuracy vs cost tradeoffs.
[03:05] Priya Raman: we'll run three variants: FP16 baseline, int8 quantized, and a higher-latency accuracy variant (e.g., larger context). for each we'll report latency, throughput, token-cost, and eval pass rate.
[03:18] Jordan Lee: and we'll include automatic fallback behavior in the acceptance tests — if latency or error rate crosses threshold Redwood will route to the fallback model, we need to validate the correctness of that fallback path.
[03:30] Carlos Mendez: good, we want to see rollback/fallback operate under simulated capacity constraints.
[03:36] Priya Raman: noted. benchmark plan summary: - 10k requests total, drawn from your traffic profile distribution (median 350 tokens, 90th 800 tokens). - run sustained throughput phase to steady-state for 30 minutes; capture P50/P95/P99 and token-level cost; - run eval pass/fail on 500 prompts; - run cold-start tests and fallback simulation.
[04:00] Aisha Khan: what's the acceptance reporting format? spreadsheet or dashboard?
[04:05] Jordan Lee: primary deliverable will be a signed acceptance report PDF + raw logs and a shared dashboard link. the dashboard will have per-route latency percentiles, error rates, token-cost breakdown, and the eval results per-prompt. we'll also attach the scripts to reproduce the run.
[04:20] Tom Wu: can you include cost modeling for projected monthly usage, say 10m tokens/month and 100k requests?
[04:28] Jordan Lee: yes we'll include a cost projection table with batch/caching assumptions.
[04:33] Carlos Mendez: one more item — availability SLA target for the POC validation should be 99.5% during the benchmark window.
[04:41] Priya Raman: we can monitor availability and include uptime percent for the window, but production SLA negotiation is separate. for the POC we'll flag any event that causes >1% error rate as a fail unless it's clearly external.
[04:54] Aisha Khan: security question again: will Redwood provide audit logs for inference requests and KMS key usage?
[05:01] Jordan Lee: yes audit logs are provided in Private and Dedicated modes; hosted will provide request-level logs masked per your PII policy. KMS usage logs are available via customer KMS when using bring-your-own-key.
[05:12] Tom Wu: perfect. ok let's talk timelines — when can you run the benchmark?
[05:16] Priya Raman: if we get artifacts (traffic profile + eval set + rubric) by Sunday we'll aim for runs starting Tuesday/Wednesday next week and final report by the following Friday.
[05:27] Carlos Mendez: that works. downtime windows are thin, we'll give you a 2-hour window for steady-state at 10am PST on Wednesday.
[05:34] Jordan Lee: noted. any competitor comparisons we should include? you mentioned Anthropic and OpenAI earlier — do you want Redwood to run a parity test vs Anthropic-lite model?
[05:44] Carlos Mendez: yes, include the model parity column if feasible. cost against OpenAI is also useful. ideally same prompts across variants.
[05:51] Priya Raman: we can run a quick parity run, licensing permitting, or rely on prior benchmark baselines if direct calls aren't allowed. we'll note differences in model versions.
[06:00] Tom Wu: thanks. this is getting granular — on the go/no-go thresholds can we write them explicitly to sign off?
[06:06] Jordan Lee: let's enumerate final go/no-go: 1) Steady-state P95 latency <= 250ms for 512-token median workload (measured with warm cache), 2) Throughput >= 120 requests/min sustained (within 10% margin), 3) Eval failure rate (hallucination/factuality) < 5% overall and no critical prompt >10% fail, 4) Cost per 1k tokens <= $0.10 with quantized variant acceptable if accuracy within 3% of FP16 baseline, 5) Availability >= 99.5% during benchmark window, 6) Fallback behavior validated (automatic routing without >2% additional errors).
[06:42] Carlos Mendez: that matches our expectations. we'll sign off if those are met in the final report.
[06:49] Aisha Khan: for reporting cadence, weekly interim reports during the POC and a final signed acceptance PDF at the end. include raw logs compressed and a CSV with token-cost breakdown.
[07:03] Priya Raman: ack. we'll produce a weekly dashboard snapshot and the final package.
[07:10] Jordan Lee: any other traps or items we missed?
[07:14] Tom Wu: legal/pricing — please send an initial SOW and pricing estimate; we may request reserved capacity if numbers look good.
[07:22] Jordan Lee: will do. I'll send pricing tiers for hosted vs dedicated and an initial SOW.
[07:28] Carlos Mendez: minor note — please annotate the report when you run quantized models which ops cause deviance from FP16, we want traceability.
[07:36] Priya Raman: we'll annotate kernels and quantization flags; also include reproducibility steps.
[07:42] Aisha Khan: ok thanks team.
[07:45] Jordan Lee: recap of next steps: Jordan sends success criteria doc + security pack; Priya schedules and runs the 10k benchmark; Acme provides traffic profile + 500 eval prompts + rubric; Tom/Legal reviews SOW. everyone good?
[07:59] Carlos Mendez: yes, good to proceed.
[08:02] Tom Wu: agree.
[08:04] Jordan Lee: great, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark window and share the doc by Monday. thanks all.
[08:09] (call ends)

Note: transcript has occasional minor transcription errors and shorthand — product names sometimes get mis-typed (e.g., "Redwood Dedicatede" or "Reedwood" in other notes).
